correctness.rationale: The source defines Lambda_n x=x_n/n on H=ℓ²(N), V_n=C. Sum ||Lambda_n x||²=Σ|x_n|²/n²≤||x||², and sup||Lambda_n||=1, satisfying the 2019 g-Bessel definition and 2020 sigma-finite counting-measure/uniform-bound assumptions. Synthesis T=diag(1/n)=T* and Gram P=T*T=diag(1/n²). x=(1/n)∈ℓ², y=Tx=(1/n²)∈R(T*); if y=Pz, then z=(1,1,...)∉ℓ². Hence universal reverse inclusion is false in both printed lemmas. For every bounded Hilbert operator T, R(P)⊆R(T*) automatically; if R(T) is closed, H_target=R(T)⊕ker(T*) gives R(T*)⊆R(P). Conversely Douglas range inclusion R(T*)⊆R(P) entails P≤λP², so its positive spectral values are ≥1/λ, and T is bounded below on ker(T)⊥, equivalent to closed range. This is an exact infinite-dimensional argument, not a finite-dimensional truncation. Both original lemma proofs were independently read, confirming they omit the closure in H_target=R(T)+ker(T*). The two downstream frame-sequence results already assume/derive closed range and are not universally declared false.
